+def _regexp_transformer(value: str) -> Pattern[str]:
+    """Transforms a regular expression.
+
+    This is not converted by default, but we need to do it for optparse-style
+    patterns to work correctly.
+    """
+    try:
+        return re.compile(value)
+    except re.error as ex:
+        # Most likely a group of unicode properties, e.g., ``\p{Han}``, that
+        # is only supported by the ``regex`` module (``re`` raises "bad
+        # escape \p" for that syntax). Fall back to the ``regex`` module
+        # for these patterns, if it is available.
+        if "\\p{" in value.lower() or "\\P{" in value:
+            try:
+                import regex
+            except ImportError:
+                raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+                    f"Error in provided regular expression: {value} beginning "
+                    f"at index {ex.pos}: {ex.msg}. This pattern appears to use "
+                    "unicode properties (e.g. \\p{Han}), which requires the "
+                    "'regex' package to be installed."
+                ) from ex
+            return regex.compile(value)  # type: ignore[return-value]
+        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+            f"Error in provided regular expression: {value} beginning at index "
+            f"{ex.pos}: {ex.msg}"
+        ) from ex
+
